title: How files become a knowledge graph
note: Traced file: concepts/Sync Engine.md. Outgoing wikilinks shown as graph edges.

intro.title: One note, from file to graph
intro.text: Ten steps through the storage layer for the Tidepool demo corpus. Step with the arrow keys or use the playback controls.

steps.title: Plain files, one library
steps.caption: Twenty-three notes in six folders make up the Tidepool demo library. The database is only an index over these markdown files.

steps.title: A note on disk
steps.caption: Writing a file is the whole write path. This scene traces concepts/Sync Engine.md from the demo corpus.

steps.title: The watcher queues it
steps.caption: The file watcher picks up changes and queues indexing. Save a note and your agent can find it in under a minute.

steps.title: Parsed into an entity
steps.caption: The parser reads frontmatter, tags, and wikilinks. The note gets a stable permalink in the local SQLite index.

steps.title: Links become edges
steps.caption: Each [[wikilink]] in Sync Engine.md resolves to a relation. Three outgoing links shown here: Conflict Resolution, Storage Layer, and 2025-11 Sync storm.

steps.title: A graph you can walk
steps.caption: Proxied tools such as build_context return a note plus its neighborhood. One hop is enough to see related decisions and incidents.

steps.title: The index is disposable
steps.caption: Delete the SQLite index and rebuild from files. Markdown stays canonical; the graph stays derived.

steps.title: One MCP surface
steps.caption: One MCP server fronts ranked search, graph walks, and every engine tool discovered at startup.

steps.title: Two read paths
steps.caption: context_search reads by similarity; build_context walks links. Both hit the same index underneath.

steps.title: Files in, knowledge out
steps.caption: The demo library compounds one markdown file at a time: searchable, linked, and current for agents.
